title: Aloo Paratha
steps: Knead a soft dough with wheat flour, water and a pinch of salt. Rest 15 minutes.
Mash potatoes and mix with chopped onion, green chilli, coriander, spices and salt for the filling.
Stuff portions of dough with the filling, seal and roll into parathas. Cook on a hot tawa with ghee until golden and crisp on both sides.
Serve hot with white butter, yogurt and pickle.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, coriander, garam masala, amchur, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Punjabi breakfast – hearty and filling.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Generous ghee and a dollop of white butter make it authentic.

title: Chole Bhature
steps: Pressure-cook chickpeas with a tea bag for dark colour. Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy with chole masala and simmer the chickpeas in it.
Knead maida with yogurt, a little oil and water into a soft dough. Rest, roll into discs and deep-fry till puffed and golden.
Serve hot bhature with chole, onion rings and pickle.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger-garlic, chole masala, tea bag (for colour)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Amritsari / Punjabi weekend breakfast or brunch.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Fluffy bhature and well-spiced chole are the hallmark.

title: Amritsari Aloo Kulcha
steps: Knead a soft dough with maida, yogurt, baking powder and water. Rest.
Prepare spiced potato filling with onion, green chilli, coriander and spices. Stuff, roll and cook in a tandoor or on a tawa until crisp and layered.
Brush with butter and serve with chole, onion and chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, coriander, nigella seeds, spices

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Amritsar's signature stuffed leavened bread – crisp outside, soft and flavourful inside.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh from a tandoor.

title: Amritsari Paneer Kulcha
steps: Knead a soft dough with maida, yogurt, baking powder and water. Rest.
Prepare spiced paneer filling with onion, green chilli, coriander and spices. Stuff, roll and cook in a tandoor or on a tawa until crisp and layered.
Brush with butter and serve with chole, onion and chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, coriander, nigella seeds, spices

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Paneer version of Amritsar's signature stuffed kulcha.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Best eaten fresh from a tandoor.

title: Sarson da Saag with Makki di Roti
steps: Wash and chop greens. Cook with ginger, garlic and green chilli till soft. Mash or blend, thicken with a little maize flour and simmer.
Temper with onion, garlic and ghee. Finish with a generous dollop of white butter.
For roti: Knead makki flour with hot water into a soft dough. Pat into thick rotis and cook on a tawa.
Serve saag hot with makki di roti and more white butter.

fullIngredients.name: Ginger, garlic, green chilli, onion, ghee, white butter

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The definitive winter comfort food of Punjab.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Slow cooking and white butter are non-negotiable.

title: Dal Makhani
steps: Soak and pressure-cook the dals till very soft. Mash lightly.
In a heavy pot melt butter, add ginger-garlic and tomato puree. Cook till oil separates. Add the dals, chilli powder and salt.
Simmer on very low heat for several hours (or overnight on a tandoor/chulha traditionally), stirring and adding cream and more butter.
Finish with a swirl of cream and serve with naan, roti or rice.

fullIngredients.name: Whole black urad dal + a little rajma

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The longer and slower it cooks, the better the flavour and creaminess.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Restaurant-style richness comes from butter and cream.

title: Kadhi Pakora
steps: Whisk yogurt with besan, turmeric and water. Cook, stirring, till it thickens and the raw smell disappears.
Make onion pakoras and deep-fry. Add them to the kadhi and simmer.
Temper with fenugreek, cumin, dry red chilli and curry leaves in ghee. Pour over.
Serve with steamed rice.

fullIngredients.name: Fenugreek seeds, cumin, dry red chilli, curry leaves, turmeric

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Thick, tangy Punjabi kadhi with soft pakoras is comfort food.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Slightly sour yogurt gives the best flavour.

title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
steps: Marinate chicken in yogurt and spices for at least 1 hour. Grill, roast or pan-sear till cooked.
In butter cook tomato puree with spices till thick. Add cream, kasuri methi and a touch of sweetness. Simmer.
Add the cooked chicken and finish with more butter and cream.
Serve with naan or rice.

fullIngredients.name: Yogurt, ginger-garlic, chilli, garam masala (for marinade)
Tomato puree, butter, cream, kasuri methi, honey or sugar

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Originated in Delhi but deeply associated with Punjabi restaurant cuisine.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mild, creamy and tomato-butter rich – not overly spicy.

title: Tandoori Chicken
steps: Make deep slits in the chicken. Marinate in the spiced yogurt mixture for several hours or overnight.
Cook in a tandoor, oven or on a grill until charred at the edges and cooked through. Baste with butter or ghee.
Serve with onion rings, lemon wedges and mint chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Yogurt, ginger-garlic, red chilli, turmeric, garam masala, lemon

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The smoky tandoor flavour is signature.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Punjab's most famous contribution to global Indian cuisine.

title: Punjabi Samosa
steps: Make a stiff dough with maida, oil and water. Rest.
Prepare spiced potato-pea filling. Shape cones from the dough, fill, seal into triangular samosas.
Deep-fry on medium heat till golden and crisp.
Serve with tamarind and green chutneys.

fullIngredients.name: Boiled potatoes, peas, spices (cumin, coriander, garam masala, amchur)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Punjabi samosas are typically larger and more generously spiced than other regional versions.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Crisp pastry and well-seasoned filling are key.

title: Onion Pakora / Mixed Pakora
steps: Mix besan with spices and water into a thick batter. Add sliced onion or chopped vegetables.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry till golden and crisp.
Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney and tea.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, potato, spinach or mixed vegetables

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Monsoon and tea-time favourite across Punjab.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Ajwain helps with digestion and adds flavour.

title: Rajma Chawal
steps: Pressure-cook soaked rajma till soft. Prepare a rich onion-tomato gravy with spices.
Add the cooked rajma and simmer till the gravy thickens and flavours meld. Finish with butter.
Serve with steamed rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Comfort food classic – the longer it simmers, the better.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often finished with a dollop of butter or cream.

title: Baingan Bharta
steps: Roast brinjals over open flame or in oven till the skin chars and flesh is soft. Peel and mash.
Temper oil with cumin, sauté onion, ginger-garlic, green chilli and tomato. Add spices.
Mix in the mashed baingan and cook till well blended. Finish with coriander.
Serve with roti or paratha.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Smoky flavour from open-flame roasting is essential.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A rustic Punjabi favourite.
